---
title: "Storefront on Start + Void"
description: "Native Storefront Worker, the cutover artifact, custom domains and Worker-version rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-21"
audience: developers
---

Storefront (`apps/storefront`) runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void behind
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge) with the React Server
Components plugin. The Next.js build (`build`) and the Vercel project are an
archived record only: rollback is a previous Cloudflare Worker version.

## Canonical host and runtime verification

`store.tuturuuu.com` is canonical. `storefront.tuturuuu.com`,
`stores.tuturuuu.com` and `storefronts.tuturuuu.com` are redirect aliases on the
same Worker. A Cloudflare response header alone does not identify a Worker.
Compare `/api/build-info` with the accepted deployment and inspect the served
HTML for native `/assets/` modules rather than Next.js `/_next/` chunks. Read
the serving Worker version from the provider; the source workflow is build-only
and cannot establish which version is live.

Build metadata can report `production` while responses still forbid indexing.
Storefront intentionally sets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` in
`start-bridge.config.ts` for every profile. `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0` does not
override that app policy. Treat search indexing as a separate product decision,
not as proof that the production profile failed to load.

## Worker profiles

| Profile | Worker | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source default (`void.config.ts`) | the staging Worker name | `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`, no routes, `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off |
| Production and cutover artifact (`VITE_STOREFRONT_NATIVE_PROFILE=production`) | `tuturuuu-storefront-wave1` | emits the production vars of `cloudflare/native-profiles.json`, with `preview_urls=false` and source map uploads off |

The Worker declares no routes. The hostname is attached at cutover by the
release operator. The Worker answers `503 Service misconfigured` (no-store)
until `INVENTORY_APP_URL`,
`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` are present
(`cloudflare/startup.ts`). Names only are recorded here.

## Request ownership

| Request | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `store.tuturuuu.com`, `storefront.tutur3u.com` | Canonical hosts. |
| `tuturuuu.com/storefront` | The production Worker serves the mount and its descendants. The gateway operator adds the binding after admission. |
| `storefront.tuturuuu.com`, `stores.tuturuuu.com`, `storefronts.tuturuuu.com` | `307` to `https://store.tuturuuu.com` with path and query preserved. |
| `/` | Redirects to `/demo`. |
| `/api/build-info` | Local build identity. |
| `/api/v1/inventory/*` | Forwarded to `INVENTORY_APP_URL`. |
| Other `/api/*` | Forwarded to `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` (default `https://tuturuuu.com`). |
| Unknown host | Rejected. |

Every response carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` from the app's
response wrapper.

## Build and artifact

`storefront-cloudflare.yaml` builds the Worker, rejects route-tree drift,
records the emitted configuration receipt, runs the emitted-Worker runtime
suites (`cloudflare/*.runtime.mjs`) and uploads `storefront-cutover-production-<source SHA>`
(14 days). The production suite runs before sealing and after a clean archive
restore. It checks the storefront demo and its emitted assets, the checkout
login return, and bounded Inventory and Web forwarding fixtures on the apex.
The archive carries no routes. Verify Inventory's scheduler handoff and the
approved checkout and payment flows before Storefront routing.

## Wave-1 production profile

`wave1-native-production.yaml` publishes a route-free upload of the sealed
production Worker; the hostname is attached later by the release owner.
`cloudflare/native-profiles.json` is the single source of the profile:

- Vars: the canonical public URLs (`https://store.tuturuuu.com`,
  `https://tuturuuu.com`), `INVENTORY_APP_URL`, `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`,
  the pinned production Supabase URL, `NODE_ENV=production` and
  `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0`.
- Required secret names: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`,
  `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`.
- `applyStorefrontNativeProfileEnv` runs before the bridge preset inlines
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`. Unset values are filled from the profile. A redirect alias
  passed as `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_STOREFRONT_APP_URL` becomes
  the canonical origin, because the publisher passes the host it attaches.
  Any other conflicting value, and the CI placeholder publishable key, fail the
  build.
- Staging stays the default profile; the staging build is unchanged.

The sealed Worker answers by host:

| Host | Every probe |
| --- | --- |
| `store.tuturuuu.com` | Build identity `200`, `/` to `/demo`, a signed-out `/orders` to `/login?next=%2Forders` on the same host, `/login` to central Web login, static assets and `robots.txt` `200`, an unknown asset `404`, an unregistered `/api/*` path `401` |
| `storefront.tuturuuu.com`, `stores.tuturuuu.com`, `storefronts.tuturuuu.com` | `307` to the same path and query on `store.tuturuuu.com`, including `/api/build-info` |
| `tuturuuu.com` | `/storefront` redirects to `/storefront/demo`, while checkout login and assets stay in the mount. Unowned paths return `404`. |
| any other host | `404 Not Found` before any app code runs |

A path that is not an asset or an API route is a storefront slug and asks
Inventory for the store, so anonymous runtime acceptance probes only asset and
API paths for unknown resources.

### Qualification commands

After `bun run --cwd apps/storefront build:cloudflare` with
`VITE_STOREFRONT_NATIVE_PROFILE=production`, the publisher's gates run in this
order. The pre-seal doctor needs the redirect-alias flag for an alias host and
the exact root redirect for the root host:

```bash
node scripts/ci/wave1-native-artifact.mjs prepare storefront production "$SHA"
node scripts/ci/pre-seal-doctor.mjs storefront apps/storefront storefront.tuturuuu.com "$SHA" --wave1 --expect-alias-of https://store.tuturuuu.com
node scripts/ci/pre-seal-doctor.mjs storefront apps/storefront store.tuturuuu.com "$SHA" --wave1 --expect-location https://store.tuturuuu.com/demo
node scripts/ci/wave1-native-runtime.mjs storefront production "$SHA"
node scripts/ci/wave1-native-publish.mjs dry-run storefront production "$SHA"
```

`wave1-native-runtime.mjs` exercises the attached host, the root host, one
alias host and an unknown host (`scripts/ci/storefront-native-runtime.mjs`).
The dry run checks the Worker upload budget; the sealed profile sets
`upload_source_maps=false`. Record the total `.map` bytes separately and keep
them below 60 MiB, even when upload is disabled. Record the gzip upload size
and scan the sealed server files for forbidden staging identities and private
files before release. A build with synthetic public inputs qualifies only the
local mechanics; production requires the approved public inputs.

## Cutover packet

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-storefront` |
| Apex mount | `tuturuuu.com/storefront` and descendants via the gateway |
| Canonical host and aliases | Worker custom domains for `store.tuturuuu.com` and the three alias hosts. |
| Static assets binding | `ASSETS` (`dist/client`, `run_worker_first`) |
| Build | Exact-commit `storefront-cloudflare.yaml` production archive |
| Secrets (names) | `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` |
| Vars | `INVENTORY_APP_URL=https://inventory.tuturuuu.com`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://store.tuturuuu.com`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL=https://tuturuuu.com` |
| Rollback | The recorded previous `tuturuuu-storefront` version; for an apex mount change, the recorded previous gateway version. |
| Data | Storefront forwards checkout writes to Inventory. The release applies no migrations. |

### Switch

1. Record the source SHA, the artifact name and the serving Worker version.
2. Provision the secrets on `tuturuuu-storefront`, deploy the artifact, and
   run the smoke below against the Worker's own address.
3. `store.tuturuuu.com` and the three alias hosts are Worker custom domains on
   `tuturuuu-storefront`. The Worker answers the alias hosts itself, so no
   separate redirect Worker is needed.

### Smoke

```bash
# Entry route and no 5xx
curl -sI https://store.tuturuuu.com/ | head -5
# Login hands off to central Web
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://store.tuturuuu.com/login
# Build identity matches the accepted SHA
curl -s https://store.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
# Alias host redirects to the canonical host
curl -sI https://storefront.tuturuuu.com/ | head -3
```

Expected: a redirect to `/demo`, a `307` to central Web login, the accepted commit, and a `307` to
`store.tuturuuu.com`.

### Alias hosts

`storefront.tuturuuu.com`, `stores.tuturuuu.com` and `storefronts.tuturuuu.com`
are custom domains on `tuturuuu-storefront`. Its app wrapper returns a `307`
preserving path and query on `https://store.tuturuuu.com`. Test `/`,
`/api/build-info` and `/orders?tag=a&tag=b` on each alias with redirects
disabled; each must redirect to the identical path and query on the canonical
host.

### Rollback

- **Triggers:** 5xx above 1% for 5 minutes, a wrong redirect, a checkout
  handoff failure, or a private store served anonymously.
- **Action:** roll `tuturuuu-storefront` back to its recorded previous Worker
  version. Custom domains stay in place; never move a host back to Vercel and
  never rebuild on the rollback path. Fix forward on Cloudflare.
- **Apex mount:** a regression in the `tuturuuu.com/storefront` mount rolls the
  gateway back to its recorded previous version.
- **Data:** a version rollback changes no catalog, order or payment data.
- **Archive:** the Vercel project and its recorded DNS records are an archived
  record only, not a rollback target. Decommissioning it is a separate approval.
